value: Full scholarship including direct and indirect cost of attendance (some restrictions may apply). Storrs campus.
deadline: Common App or Coalition Application by November 1, 2026. Day of Pride Supplemental Application and all required documents by November 8, 2026.

application: Apply for admission by November 1, then submit the Day of Pride supplement by November 8 with short responses of 100, 200 and 100 words, a detailed resume and two recommendations. Interviews may be required. Choose only one of Day of Pride, Nutmeg or Stamps.

eligibility: Connecticut residents graduating from a Connecticut secondary school and enrolling at Storrs in fall 2027. Applicants must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or undocumented student resident in Connecticut for at least two years, with at least a 3.6 GPA on a 4.0 scale and top 15% class rank if available. Leadership, community contributions and documented financial need are considered. Optional submitted scores should be SAT 1170 or ACT 24. Up to 20 recipients.

supports: identity: Dickinson College confirms Music Scholars Award.
value: Covers one full credit of private studio lessons each semester (up to $1,500 annually or $6,000 over four years)
deadline: Submit SlideRoom materials by the admission deadline. For fall 2027 admission: Early Decision I and Early Action November 15, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.

application: Submit SlideRoom materials through the Common Application. Instrumentalists and vocalists submit two solo video performances, preferably contrasting styles; audio-only and nonsolo ensemble videos are not accepted. Composers submit PDFs of two contrasting compositions, with recordings optional. Music history, theory or ethnomusicology applicants submit a PDF writing sample, with original multimedia optional. Awards are announced with the admission decision.
eligibility: Prospective first-year students with musical talent; recipients do not need to major in music.

eligibility: Sunderman is for music majors; Wagnild is for music majors, minors and occasionally highly talented nonmajors. Headley Paul is described as an award for an enrolled music-degree student, with keyboard/piano preference. All require an audition.

Write an original 700-800-word nonfiction essay on Finding My Voice in a World Full of Noise. Double-space, single-sided, number pages; separate identifying title page, anonymous essay body, citations and manual word count. English, or French/Spanish accepted by the district. Limited adult guidance permitted; originality certified and plagiarism/AI checks used. Club winner advances to district.

eligibility: Under 19 on October 1, 2026, with no minimum age; secondary school/equivalent not yet completed, including CEGEP students. Enter in district of residence; U.S. military-installation pupils abroad may use last U.S. home of record. Non-districted places without a club are ineligible. Previous district Essay scholarship winners may never reenter.

supports: identity: Writers of the Future confirms Writers of the Future Contest.

value: Quarterly cash prizes $1,000/$750/$500, paid within 60 days of announcement. Quarterly first winners compete for an additional $5,000 annual cash prize. Winners offered travel/hotel for annual ceremony and free writing workshop.
deadline: Recurring quarterly cutoffs: December 31, March 31, June 30 and September 30, midnight Pacific Time; postal postmark or electronic receipt. Late work moves to following quarter.

application: Submit one original English speculative-fiction prose manuscript per quarter online or by mail, with anonymous double-spaced numbered pages and separate contact/word-count information. Short story under 10,000 words or novelette under 17,000; no AI-generated content, already published work, fanfiction or nonspeculative work. No entry fee; no revisions after submission.

eligibility: New/amateur writers who have not professionally published a novel/short novel, more than one novelette, or more than three short stories. Professional means at least eight cents/word and at least 5,000 copies/hits. Any quarterly prize winner cannot enter again; unchanged repeated submissions become ineligible. Void where prohibited by law; rules impose no age restriction.

supports: identity: Civil Air Patrol confirms CAP Cadet Academic Scholarships (CadetInvest).

deadline: Applications are projected to open December 15, 2026 at noon Central and close January 15, 2027 at noon Central, including unit and wing approval.

application: In e-Services Registration Zone, submit the primary Scholarship application and at least one academic scholarship subevent, a resume of no more than two pages and one to three recommendations about your CAP accomplishments. eligibility: Current active CAP cadets in good standing, with the Billy Mitchell Award or higher, who are high school seniors, graduates or GED holders and have applied to or been accepted by a postsecondary school. Individual awards add requirements: Etheridge requires a B average; Schroder requires a STEM major and original essay; August Trust is for Arizona Wing STEM or aviation cadets; Diaz is restricted to listed Florida squadrons; Mullins is need-based for Michigan Wing cadets.

supports: identity: ASHRAE confirms ASHRAE High School Senior Scholarships.

value: Four one-year scholarships of $3,000. Awards are capped at direct annual education costs; only one Society scholarship may be received per year. Former applicants and recipients may reapply if eligible.

application: Submit one online application, professional-goals and HVAC&R-involvement answers, a financial-need statement, an official transcript sent directly by the school, college acceptance evidence and three signed recommendations from an instructor/advisor, employer and nonfamily character reference. Arrange a local ASHRAE chapter interview and evaluation; applicants under 18 need parent authorization. AI use is prohibited.

eligibility: High school seniors entering full time into a bachelor’s-level pre-engineering, engineering or engineering technology program preparing for HVAC&R work. Require at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale OR top-30% class standing. The institution must host an active ASHRAE student branch, have ABET accreditation or an ABET memorandum, or qualifying international accreditation under the Washington or Sydney Accord. Financial need, character, leadership, service and professional potential are considered. Students already receiving full educational funding from an employer, military or other organization are excluded.

supports: identity: Music Teachers National Association (MTNA) confirms Senior Brass and Voice Performance Competitions.
value: National Winner $2,000, Second $1,000, Third $500, Merit Awards $100 (separately for brass and voice)
deadline: Registration opens November 1, 2026 on Acceptd; video deadline December 2, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. ET

application: Register on Acceptd from November 1, 2026 and upload unedited, fixed-camera performance videos by December 2 at 3 PM Eastern. Show the performer’s full body and instrument, with the live pianist visible where accompaniment is required; YouTube links are not accepted. Submit all registered repertoire, which cannot change between rounds. Seven finalists per category perform live in St. Louis; the senior rehearsal, competition and winners’ concert are April 2, 3 and 4, 2027.

eligibility: Brass players (trumpet, horn, euphonium, trombone or tuba) and singers ages 15 to 18 on January 1, 2027, studying with a teacher. Entrants must reside in the U.S. during the competition year and be U.S. citizens, valid U.S. visa holders, asylees or permanent residents. Under-18 entrants need parent permission. Previous national first-place winners cannot reenter the same level and category.

supports: identity: National Federation of Music Clubs (NFMC) confirms Stillman Kelley National Instrumental Awards and Thelma Byrum Piano Award.

supports: identity: National Federation of Music Clubs (NFMC) confirms Michael R. Edwards Graduating Senior Performance Award.
value: $5,000, paid in two $2,500 installments after first- and second-semester enrollment verification.

application: Submit the NFMC online application and all materials together, including the performance submission, two recommendations and music-school acceptance for the immediate academic year. Repertoire requires three contrasting periods and one American composition. Pay the $20 fee online.

eligibility: Graduating high school seniors under 19 by May 1 who will pursue a music performance degree at an accredited music school and have earned at least one NFMC Federation Cup. NFMC Junior membership and U.S. citizenship are required. Prior first-place winners cannot reenter the same award.

supports: identity: National Federation of Music Clubs (NFMC) confirms Lynn Freeman Olson Composition Awards.
value: $1,500 high-school and $750 intermediate awards for further musical study; judges may withhold awards.

application: Follow the award-specific mailed application rules: send the typed signed form, an original manuscript and six legible copies, postmarked by March 1 in an odd year. Do not email or upload. Submit one anonymous piano solo or piano-only ensemble composition, no more than four engraved pages and written for early-elementary to intermediate piano skill. Do not include recordings.

eligibility: Nonprofessional composers in grades 10 to 12 for the $1,500 high-school category, or grades 7 to 9 for the $750 intermediate category, who are currently studying music and are NFMC members. Works must not have been published for public use or sale. Only one original composition per entrant; arrangements are excluded. Past monetary winners cannot reenter the same category. U.S. citizenship is not required.

supports: identity: Bennington College confirms Bennington Young Creators Awards (Young Artists, Innovators, Musicians and Scientists).

value: Cash prizes in each discipline: First $2,000, Second $1,000, Third $500, Distinguished $250. If enrolling at Bennington: First Place full tuition for four years, Distinguished half tuition for four years, Finalists $25,000 per year for four years.
deadline: 2026-27 cycle: opens September 1, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Eastern; closes November 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. Winners announced in spring 2027.

application: Submit one entry per discipline, choosing one category within it, with sponsoring teacher/mentor review and approval. Grades 9 to 11 use the YCA registration/portal; grade 12 first submits a nonbinding Common or Coalition Application to Bennington, then receives YCA instructions. Artists: one 2D image, up to three 3D images, or 1 to 2 minute digital work; optional description up to 500 words. Musicians: one original composition up to five minutes; recording/MIDI strongly recommended, optional score/lyrics, English translation for other-language lyrics. Scientists: a natural-science visual artifact, up to five PDF/images, optional explanation up to 500 words. Innovators: AI creative work plus 500 to 750 word reflection, a critical essay up to 1,200 words plus AI-use note up to 300 words if applicable, or a practical AI project with video up to three minutes and explanation up to 500 words.
eligibility: Students in grades 9 to 12 worldwide; graduated students are not eligible.

identity: South Carolina Commission on Higher Education confirms LIFE Scholarship.

Eligible SC schools/homeschool or qualified out-of-state dependent route applies; later college eligibility can be earned with LIFE GPA/credit requirements. Enhancement requires approved major and normally 14 eligible math/science/accounting credits by end of first college year; education route has separate service-contract requirements.

deadline.note: No separate statewide scholarship application deadline; official rules assign document/admission deadlines to the institution, including the early-graduation route.

application.note: College determines eligibility using official final high-school transcript, residency/citizenship verification and any applicable test/rank documentation. Mid-year applicants provide principal/counselor certification and early-graduation documents.

eligibility.note: South Carolina resident and U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident at high-school graduation and college enrolment; minimum 3.0 unrounded SC Uniform Grading Policy GPA at graduation; first-time full-time degree student at eligible four-year institution who does not receive LIFE or Palmetto Fellows. Approved homeschool and qualified out-of-state dependent graduates can qualify with UGP transcript conversion as applicable; GED graduates are not eligible for initial HOPE. Normally at least 12 non-remedial/non-continuing-education credits; approved disability exceptions exist.

application: Submit FAFSA for academic year immediately following graduation, or TOPS Online Application only if family finances make applicant ineligible for federal grant aid. Save receipt and match name/date-of-birth across transcript and testing records. LOSFA may request official academic records, residency affidavit and citizenship/PR documentation; homeschool registration and prior-school records need verification. Send official scores using LOSFA codes (ACT 1595, SAT 9019; select LOSFA/TOPS for CLT), monitor Student Hub and respond to requests. FAFSA renewal normally annual; initial TOPS-only applicants do not refile that form annually.

deadline: Full-award application receipt: July 1, or next business day, following one-year anniversary of high-school graduation. FAFSA priority February 1 of senior year. All initial-eligibility documentation due January 15 following final application deadline. Current testing guidance requires April national ACT/CLT deadline and March SAT deadline in graduation year to avoid reduced eligibility; later qualifying tests before August 1 normally reduce funding by one semester/two quarters. Exact 2027 testing days/time zone not stated; special military/out-of-state-return deadlines apply.

changes.before: Louisiana resident; U.S. citizen or permanent resident; BESE-approved high school; 19.0 units of the TOPS Core Curriculum. Opportunity: 2.50 TOPS core GPA and ACT of at least the prior-year state average but never less than 20. Performance: 3.25 core GPA and ACT 23. Honors: 3.50 core GPA and ACT 27 (SAT equivalents accepted). Must enroll full time by the first semester after the first anniversary of graduation.
changes.after: Standard approved-school route: 19 TOPS core units with core GPA 2.50 for Opportunity, 3.25 Performance or 3.50 Honors; ACT respectively prior-year Louisiana average (never below 20), 23 or 27. Opportunity threshold is set annually. Current homeschool guidance instead uses ACT 20/23/27 or specified SAT/CLT equivalents without the core/GPA route; older award pages still show higher homeschool scores. Eligible out-of-state-school route uses higher ACT scores 23/26/30 in lieu of core/GPA. U.S. citizen or permanent resident at graduation; pending prior-to-graduation permanent-residency application requires LOSFA review and cannot be paid until approved. Louisiana residency normally established through final two school years or 24-month student/parent/legal-guardian residency; qualified military exceptions exist. Confirm graduation-year core and test rules with LOSFA.
changes.reason: Corrected or qualified after reading current official program content.

changes.before: Only usable at eligible Louisiana institutions. ACT superscores are not accepted. Out-of-state and home study graduates have different score requirements.
changes.after: Only eligible Louisiana institutions. ACT superscores not accepted. Annual full-time/continuous enrolment and normally 24 earned academic-year credits required; all college coursework, including dual enrolment, affects GPA. Opportunity renewal needs 2.30 at 24-47 hours then 2.50; Performance/Honors/Excellence need 3.00 at annual review, with intermediate steady-progress conditions. Higher awards can revert permanently to Opportunity after GPA shortfall. GPA suspension can be restored within allowed period; approved medical/military exceptions concern enrolment/credits. National Guard has separate tuition-exemption/book benefits and larger education stipends; check award-specific rules. Remaining eligibility may fund graduate/professional study under enrolment rule, not a second bachelor degree.

supports: identity: Kentucky Higher Education Assistance Authority (KHEAA) confirms Kentucky Educational Excellence Scholarship (KEES).

value: Each qualifying high-school year earns $187 at 2.75 GPA to $500 at 4.00 toward each college year; earned annual base amounts accumulate. Highest pregraduation ACT/SAT bonus up to $500; free/reduced-lunch eligible students can add $200-$300 per qualifying AP/IB/Cambridge examination, with no examination-count cap. Half-time college enrolment minimum; part-time amounts adjusted. Award expires at eight funded semesters, five years after graduation or bachelor degree, whichever first. Separate comprehensive-transition programme awards for students with intellectual disabilities are $250/$500 per term based on load, up to eight terms.

eligibility: Kentucky resident, U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident; not a convicted felon. Certified-school GPA route needs approved curriculum and at least 2.75 in an award-earning year beginning 2026-27. Kentucky homeschool/noncertified-school graduates and qualifying GED recipients (age 18-23) can earn a score-only award, without the school GPA route. Certain Kentucky-resident military dependents, exchange/Page School students and approved programmes outside Kentucky qualify.

application: No separate application for ordinary college route: school reports grades, test results and eligibility; check MyKHEAA records and college financial-aid office. Approved workforce reimbursement instead requires Pathway Selection Form, request form and clear itemised receipts after eligible expenses are paid.

supports: identity: Nevada State Treasurer (NVigate) confirms Governor Guinn Millennium Scholarship.

value: Up to $10,000 lifetime tuition benefit, paid per credit up to 15 credits each semester: $40 lower/$60 upper division at NSHE community colleges, $60 Nevada State University, $80 other eligible institutions. Remedial/graduate courses excluded; student pays uncovered costs. Normally six years after high-school graduation, with military/service/disability extensions. Institution credits account; summer often requires upfront payment and later reimbursement.

application: Traditional school reports eligible students; award packet normally mailed July/August, then student must acknowledge award online and complete citizenship affidavit. Enrol in recognised eligible degree/certificate programme with 12 university/state-college or nine community-college credits. Homeschool/out-of-state applicants use linked form with signed application, official sealed transcript if applicable, official ACT/SAT results, residency/dependency documents and homeschool district-waiver documentation as applicable.
eligibility: Traditional and citizenship/renewal guidance fully read. Linked homeschool/out-of-state forms are dated October 2019, so route-specific 2027 requirements need confirmation.

deadline: Traditional school route has no separate application. Linked nontraditional forms refer to Board of Regents graduation-year limitations, without a 2027 schedule; those route-specific limits were not confirmed.

supports: identity: West Virginia Higher Education Policy Commission confirms PROMISE Scholarship.

value: Up to $5,500 per year or eligible tuition/mandatory fees, whichever less; maximum determined annually and funding contingent on state appropriations. Institution receives payment for degree-pursuant undergraduate coursework. Up to eight bachelor semesters or four associate semesters; normally must use within six years after award, with military extension. Completion of degree ends eligibility. Renewal normally 2.75 overall college GPA and 30 earned credits per two-semester academic year (15 for one semester), continuous full-time enrolment, with final-year exceptions.

deadline: Class of 2027: Promise application and 2027-28 FAFSA open October 1, 2026; both must meet submission/processing conditions by March 1, 2027. Last qualifying SAT administration is June 2027; last qualifying national ACT is July 2027. No time zone stated.

application: Create WVSAM account, verify email, submit Promise application and 2027-28 FAFSA by March 1, 2027, even if qualifying grades/scores are still pending. Send individual official test administrations (ACT code 4539, SAT 3456) and monitor matching/status. Public-school academic records generally supplied through school system; private-school final records and special homeschool/commuter/military forms require school/applicant verification. Scholars do not reapply annually; annual FAFSA encouraged for other aid.

eligibility: Class of 2027: overall high-school GPA at least 3.0/B under approved school policy; separate core GPA requirement removed. ACT composite 21 on English/reading/math or SAT 1080; superscores accepted beginning 2027-28, without mixing ACT/SAT formats. U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen. Student AND FAFSA parent/legal guardian normally need 12 consecutive months WV residency before deadline; at least half high-school credits completed at qualifying WV school and eligible graduation route. Qualified homeschool/Hope-IIP, daily out-of-state commuter, military and approved alternative-education routes require additional documents. First-time full-time initial award normally within two years of graduation, with specified exceptions.

supports: identity: Boettcher Foundation confirms Boettcher Scholarship.

value: $20,000 annually from Boettcher for four consecutive undergraduate years. Public partners supplement up to cost of attendance minus travel/other expenses; private partners supplement up to tuition/fees. Partner support and legal-status eligibility can vary; good standing and continuing lawful presence/status required.
deadline: Recurring stages and 5 p.m. cutoff confirmed; current cycle year and time zone not explicitly published.

application: Complete online application, essays and activity information. Arrange counselor forms and official transcript within one week after submission; scores optional. Semifinalists provide two recommendation letters; finalists interview. Noncitizens provide status/application evidence at semifinal stage and approved lawful-presence/status documentation and affirmation before award; renew documentation annually.

eligibility: Graduating Colorado high-school student applying in fall of final high-school year, normally Colorado resident for full junior/senior years; federally recognized tribal members with historical Colorado ties have a residency exception. Colorado high-school graduation still required. U.S. citizen, permanent resident or lawfully present, including DACA; applicants in process must document successful status before becoming a Scholar. Relatives of Foundation trustees/officers/employees excluded under published criteria. Merit selection considers academics, leadership, service and character, without financial-need preference.
